findings.summary: Most deliverables were already in the base, so the candidate is mainly tests plus the captain wording fix.
findings.evidence: Only intro.json and site.rs changed. The base already had the Athena header, the Next steps section, source links, the plain f2 text in findings.json, and the docs and CHANGELOG entries (CHANGELOG.md:29, docs/design/explainer-site.md:27). summary: The code change meets criteria 1–6. Read together with the base, the page leads with Athena, says this page is an example study of firstmate, and says who uses firstmate and that its workers are AI agents. The captain glossary entry now says what the study does and does not establish. The page has a Next steps section linking to both repositories, every claim source links to its file and lines at the pinned commit with escaped text, and the f2 limit is in plain language. New named tests cover each of these, and all of them pass. I ran cargo test -p xtask, cargo clippy --all-targets, cargo fmt --check and a full cargo test, and all passed. The site build wrote index.html under the configured target directory and left the work tree clean. Policy blocked reading the built file directly, so I confirmed its content through tests that render the real study with the same code. Criterion 7, the producer's report with its evidence table, is not in the snapshot and I could not check it, so I marked it unmet; that is the only reason the verdict is fail. If Athena confirms the report has the table and the gate results, the change otherwise passes. There are two minor findings: the next-steps test is too weak to catch a missing firstmate link, and the CHANGELOG was not updated for the captain wording change.
